children: What an hour here feels like
You arrive to warm tea and a room already dim and quiet. No forms to rush through, no small talk you don’t want. Just a slow start and a therapist who lets the hour set its own pace.

Warm oil, unhurried pressure, and the particular stillness that only comes when someone else is minding the time for once. You leave loose, warm, and a little further from the morning than you thought possible.

pages.name: About
pages.seoDescription: Who Stillwater is, what we do and the people behind the work.

children.class: mx-auto grid w-full max-w-5xl items-center gap-10 @3xl:grid-cols-2 @3xl:gap-16

attrs.alt: A quiet lounge with low light, plants and a pot of tea

children: We opened Stillwater because rest had started to feel like something you had to earn. We wanted a room where you didn’t — where the light was already low, the towels already warm, and no one was watching the clock but us.

It’s a small retreat on purpose. A handful of rooms, a few therapists who’ve worked together for years, and a pace that never speeds up. Come as you are, tired as you are. That’s exactly who this is for.

children.class: mx-auto flex w-full max-w-5xl flex-col gap-10

children: Your room, your hour, your quiet. We never double-book a therapist or hurry the changeover between guests.
Warm oils and essential blends we’d use ourselves — nothing harsh, nothing you’ll smell all day unless you want to.
Deep or feather-light, chatty or silent — you tell us at the start, and we follow it the whole way through.
